mentions.name: Tmux-style web browser
mentions.description: This is a web browser with tmux/iTerm2-style tabs and panes that can save window configurations and tab contents to a file checked into projects and loaded back as source-controlled views, letting developers keep project documentation links and local development browser tools (like database viewers) in dedicated views. Features include a Chrome-devtools-style viewport manager, a session manager that treats browser sessions as first-class entities with attach/detach tabs and an incognito toggle, a system light/dark override for testing appearance modes, a reload trigger that reloads one tab when a target tab reloads, and a structured log file viewer with search/filter and play/pause. It emphasizes keyboard-driven navigation via a global nav mode toggle for moving between panes and tabs, with planned features including screenshot/video capture and 'tab links' that sync navigation of shared tabs across multiple views.
mentions.problem: The author always wanted a browser with tmux/iTerm2-style tabs/panes because daily-driver browsers and OS window managers force people to hack side-by-side views together; alternatives like Zen have split panes but not the robust tab/panel system wanted, and flipping the OS light/dark setting to test modes is tedious.
mentions.audience: Daily-driver browser users and developers who juggle project documentation, local dev tools, and side-by-side views
mentions.source_excerpt: I have always wanted a web browser with tmux/iterm2 style tabs/panes, as well as the ability to save the window configuration and tab contents to a file that can be checked in to projects and loaded.
mentions.author: corytheboyd
